Want real hands-on experience in B2B SaaS marketing — running webinars, shaping demand gen campaigns, and building the AI-powered systems that run our marketing team? Then it's an exciting time to join Luminovo!

We help electronics manufacturers and OEMs manage one of the most complex supply chains in the world by bringing sourcing, quoting, and procurement into a single, modern platform. title: React Native Developer
description:

Tasks

What You'll Be Doing

You'll take significant ownership of our app's architecture and user experience. You'll make the key calls on architecture, state management, API integration and performance monitoring, together with the engineers who built the rest of our platform. The API is stable, the backend is mature and most of the feature logic is already proven in our responsive web version, so you're building the mobile layer on a system that works rather than starting from zero. It also means the app won't be a 1:1 copy of the web product, and figuring out what mobile should actually be is a large part of the job.

  • Own the product beyond the interface: You'll take full accountability for your features end to end. That means managing complex local state, building smooth user journeys and ensuring native-level performance. You'll write, ship and iterate on your own code.
  • Design scalable, smart architecture: You'll build a robust mobile foundation using patterns like MVVM or TCA that connect seamlessly with our Effect-based backend and AI systems. Expect to take on tough engineering challenges around real-time synchronization, offline-first capabilities and streaming AI responses.
  • Keep the technical bar high: You'll track down and fix performance issues like sluggish render cycles or slow app startup times. At the same time, you'll push for better maintainability, strict type safety and a consistent UX across the codebase.

Tech Stack

  • Mobile: TypeScript, React Native, Expo

If you don't know every tool here from day one, that's fine. We trust your ability to pick things up quickly.

Requirements

What We're Looking For

  • Solid experience with TypeScript and React Native, including apps you've shipped to the stores and maintained afterwards. You know what OTA updates, native module issues and a rejected store review feel like in practice.
  • End-to-End Ownership: You don't throw things over the wall. You own your features until they're running successfully in production and used by real learners.
  • Not a lone wolf: You'll be our main mobile person, but you won't be working in isolation. You'll sit close to the backend and product engineers, and you should enjoy defending your technical decisions and changing your mind when someone makes a better case.

title: Lead / Senior Commercial Steering & Planning Manager (B2B) (f/m/d)
description:
About the role

Zenjob's B2B business grows through three motions: winning new customers, rolling out more of their locations, and expanding volume in the locations we already serve.

We can see that growth today. What we can't yet see is how much of it was actually available to us — whether a vertical captured its potential or simply beat an easy comparison. That question has no owner, and no denominator.

You'll build both. You own commercial steering for the B2B business — the numbers the CEO, Commercial Management and CFO decide on, and the baseline that makes those numbers mean something.

What you'll work on

  • Commercial steering. Making the B2B organisation steerable: one consistent set of numbers across four verticals, a metrics framework people trust, and early warning before a drift shows up in a quarterly result. Dashboards are how it's delivered, not what the job is.

  • The potential baseline. Locations, shift volume and staffing budget per customer — so growth is measured against what was there, not against last year.

  • Where capacity goes. The other half of the growth question: whether AM time and sales focus sit on the accounts that justify them. You'll track coverage against potential and revenue per AM hour, and work with the Vertical Heads to rebalance portfolios when they don't line up.

  • Forecasting and planning. Existing demand, new pipeline and expansion modelled as three separate lines instead of one blended number — plus a unit-economics-driven, bottom-up revenue plan built together with Finance.

  • Targets, incentives and accountability. The target and incentive logic across all four verticals — quota design, bonus mechanics, accelerators — together with the funnel reviews where verticals are held to it. One loop: what we ask for, what we pay for, and where we check. It only works if every rep can explain how their own number comes about.

  • From finding to fix. Your analysis doesn't stop at the insight. You work out what's actually driving a gap, hand it to the function that can close it — Enablement for a skill or process fix, our project office for a structural one — and then measure whether it worked.

  • The marketplace view. A standing interface with your B2C Steering counterpart, so commercial ambition stays connected to what we can actually fulfill.

What you'll bring

  • 4–7 years in commercial analytics, revenue operations, sales strategy or something comparable — ideally B2B SaaS, marketplace or staffing.

  • You've owned reporting end-to-end, not just contributed to someone else's.

  • You build forecasting and planning models comfortably, and you can defend what they say.

  • You can explain a complex commercial dynamic to someone who doesn't work with numbers all day.

  • You'd rather build the first version of something than maintain the tenth.

Why this one is interesting

Most steering roles inherit a system and keep it running. This one builds it — you'll define how a four-vertical commercial organisation measures itself, with direct access to the CEO, Commercial Managmenet and CFO.

The remit is deliberately clear rather than all-encompassing: pricing sits with Finance, supply steering with your B2C counterpart, cross-functional project delivery with our Commercial Mgmt Office. Your job is the numbers, and what they tell us to do next.

Deine Aufgaben:

title: Product Engineer — Working Student
description:
Working Student - Product Engineer

Over 4 million merchants use our card readers to process payments in 34 countries. As we build a world where every business can thrive, we continually expand our range of products and services. We are a truly global fintech company, with 3,000+ people from 93 nationalities spread across 22 offices on four continents.

As the People Tech team, our mission is to enable long-term scalability by fostering a data-informed culture through seamless systems and a people-centric employee experience. As our Product Engineer - Working Student, your first mission will be to help us rethink Feedback and Team Reviews: learn how the process works today, find the friction and turn promising ideas into product experiences that colleagues can test.

The work starts frontend-first: build realistic prototypes in React, Next.js or similar and explore a simpler product layer over Workday, our system of record. If a direction proves valuable, you may help grow it into a standalone internal app - from interface and APIs to data models, authentication and integrations - alongside People Tech and engineering partners.

This is a real product challenge, not a side quest: you will learn across discovery, UX, frontend, testing and product decisions, supported by mentorship and code review. You will collaborate with Product Owners, process owners, people tech and workday specialists, sumuppers, managers, people partners, people analytics and senior stakeholders, with potential exposure to backend development, integrations and production delivery. If your favourite way to answer "what if?" is to build it, you will fit right in.

What you'll do

  • Find the right problem: Speak with process owners, employees and managers to understand Feedback and Team Reviews, identify friction and decide what is worth solving first.
  • Shape a focused product slice: Turn requirements, questions and constraints into clear user journeys and an MVP that can teach us something useful.
  • Prototype and iterate quickly: Build realistic frontend experiences in React, Next.js or similar; compare directions, test assumptions and adjust when the evidence points somewhere better.
  • Design for different kinds of work:  Create accessible, intuitive flows for office-based teams, metrics-driven Field Sales colleagues and on-site teams without building three separate products.
  • Think end to end:  If the concept is validated, help evolve it towards a standalone app while considering APIs, data, authentication, privacy, deployment, integrations and what should remain in Workday.
  • Use AI as a co-pilot, not an alibi:  Use tools such as Cursor, GitHub Copilot, v0, Lovable or similar to accelerate development while still understanding, checking and owning the result.
  • Make the learning visible: Demo your work, explain decisions and trade-offs, respond to feedback and document the findings and technical choices that should shape the next version.

You'll be great for this role if

  • Student status. You are currently enrolled at a university and available for a part-time role based in Berlin.
  • Modern web development skills. You have built web applications with React, Next.js or a similar frontend framework. Coursework, internships, hackathons, personal projects and portfolio work all count.
  • Product-minded builder. You care about the user's goal and accessibility, and can turn an ambiguous problem into the simplest useful solution, test it and iterate.
  • Full-stack and AI curiosity. You want to learn how APIs, data and services turn an interface into a reliable product, and can use AI-assisted tools while still understanding, checking and owning the result.
  • Clear, team-first communication. You can explain what you built end to end, make technical choices understandable, ask for input and respond well to feedback.

Nice to have

  • Backend and integration foundations. Some experience with Node.js, TypeScript, Python, databases, APIs, serverless functions, Supabase, Firebase, AWS or comparable technologies.
  • Identity and data concepts. A basic understanding of OAuth, SSO, permissions or responsible data handling.
  • What we don't expect: years of professional experience, previous Workday knowledge or a perfect first attempt. If you do not tick every box, please apply anyway and show us what you can build, how you think and how you learn.

description:

You will collaborate closely with silicon, firmware, software, power, mechanical, thermal and manufacturing teams, as well as external suppliers and technology partners, to deliver reliable, high-performance products.

This is an excellent opportunity for an engineer who enjoys combining hands-on hardware development with cross-functional collaboration to solve challenging technical problems.

  • Support the development of accelerator boards and platform hardware throughout the full product lifecycle, from concept to production.
  • Contribute to hardware architecture, schematic reviews, design integration and technical trade-off analysis.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional engineering teams to ensure successful hardware implementation and system integration.
  • Review schematics, PCB layouts, manufacturing documentation and engineering changes.
  • Support component selection, qualification, lifecycle management and supply chain readiness.
  • Drive hardware bring-up, debugging, root-cause analysis and board validation activities.
  • Develop and execute functional, electrical and system-level validation plans.
  • Investigate and resolve hardware, firmware, manufacturing and system integration issues.
  • Support Design for Manufacturing (DFM), Design for Assembly (DFA), Design for Test (DFT) and broader Design for Excellence (DFX) activities.
  • Work with manufacturing partners, suppliers and technology vendors throughout product development.
  • Support EMC, safety and regulatory compliance activities.
  • Contribute to technical planning, project execution, risk assessment and engineering

Qualifications & Skills:

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering or a related discipline.
  • Experience in board-level hardware development, hardware validation, system integration or a related engineering role.
  • Ability to read and understand schematics, PCB layouts, manufacturing documentation and component datasheets.
  • Good understanding of digital hardware design, PCB development and hardware bring-up methodologies.
  • Hands-on experience with laboratory equipment such as oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, power supplies, electronic loads and digital multimeters.
  • Familiarity with embedded systems and firmware-hardware interactions.
  • Strong analytical, troubleshooting and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent communication skills and ability to work effectively in multidisciplinary teams.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience developing server, networking, accelerator or data center hardware platforms.
  • Knowledge of high-speed interfaces such as PCIe, DDR, Ethernet, SPI, I²C/SMBus and UART.
  • Experience with Siemens Xpedition or similar PCB design tools.
  • Understanding of Signal Integrity (SI), Power Integrity (PI) and high-speed PCB design principles.
  • Experience with silicon bring-up, board validation or system integration.
  • Knowledge of EMC/EMI design practices and regulatory compliance.
  • Experience working with PCB manufacturers, assembly partners and component suppliers.
  • Basic scripting or automation skills using Python, Shell or similar languages.
  • Familiarity with product lifecycle management and engineering change processes.
  • Experience in AI, HPC or accelerator hardware environments.

title: Manager_Associate Director - Project Management
description:
About Relation

Relation is a sector defining TechBio company developing transformational medicines, with technology at our core. Our ambition is to understand human biology in unprecedented ways, discovering therapies to treat some of life’s most devastating diseases. We leverage single-cell multi-omics from patient tissue, functional assays, and machine learning to drive disease understanding, from cause to cure.

We are scaling rapidly and building a team of exceptional individuals to push the boundaries of drug discovery. You will work in highly interdisciplinary teams where biology, computation, and engineering come together to solve complex problems that have not been solved before. Our state-of-the-art wet and dry labs in the heart of London are designed to accelerate this integration and translate insight into impact.

We are committed to building diverse and inclusive teams. Relation is an equal opportunities employer and does not discriminate on the basis of gender, sexual orientation, marital or civil partnership status, gender reassignment, race, colour, nationality, ethnic or national origin, religion or belief, disability, or age.

By joining Relation, you will help define how medicines are discovered and deliver meaningful impact for patients.

The opportunity

Relation is offering an outstanding opportunity for an experienced Project Manager to work in close partnership with our Programme and Project Leaders, putting you in a prime position to help shape delivery plans and drive our osteoporosis programme forward.

Working across the full discovery journey, you'll help move the programme through Target ID, Hit-to-Lead, Lead Optimisation, Candidate Selection and beyond — coordinating across the multiple projects that make up the programme, our internal interdisciplinary teams, and third-party partners such as CROs, all while navigating the ambiguity of discovery-stage science with confidence.

You'll operate at programme level, with visibility across every project within the osteoporosis programme, partnering with the Programme Leader and the Project Leaders who own each individual project. If this sounds like you, and you thrive in matrixed environments and want a real hand in shaping how tomorrow's medicines are discovered, come and join us in the heart of London.

Day to day, you will

  • Partner with Programme, Project Leaders and sponsors to understand the strategic objectives and delivery requirements across the programme.

  • Orchestrate the matrix team to deliver against project objectives, motivating all team members with clear direction and communication.

  • Work with functional leads to ensure appropriate resource allocation and to onboard supplementary resources where needed to support delivery.

  • Proactively manage plans, budgets, risks and issues across the programme, escalating to senior management when appropriate.

  • Support leadership in navigating high-impact, high-risk situations with clear analysis, high transparency and a spirit of partnership — even in the face of significant adversity or major obstacles.

  • Translate scientific and strategic objectives into integrated project plans, timelines and milestones.

  • Coordinate execution across the wet lab, ML research, data science and engineering teams, owning cross-team dependencies and prioritisation, and actively monitoring interdependencies across teams as the programme evolves.

title: IT Security Specialist
description:
What is the job?

Montu UK is entering an exciting new phase in its security journey: creating an independent, future-ready architecture for the UK and Europe. We’re moving beyond shared APAC infrastructure to establish our own tenants, controls and security ecosystem -built specifically for the unique demands of our rapidly growing UK and EU operations.

Australia has already developed a mature security architecture; this role is an opportunity to take that strong foundation and shape it for an entirely different regulatory and operational landscape. You’ll build security around requirements including CQC, GPhC, MHRA, Home Office controlled drugs, UK GDPR and NHS DSPT, while supporting an expanding estate that includes our Winnersh Triangle site, EU tenant separation and continued European growth.

This is not a governance-only role focused on auditing, reporting or writing policies - we already have dedicated teams owning that work. We need a hands-on security builder: someone who can design, implement and operate meaningful controls, solve complex technical challenges and strengthen our security capabilities from the inside.

You’ll work directly alongside the IT Manager as a close collaborator on both strategy and delivery, with the Support Analyst and HiLabs Ireland contact forming your wider working circle. You’ll be part of the team building and delivering the architecture -not standing outside it and checking the work.

Given the regulatory responsibility Montu carries, sound judgement and trustworthiness are essential - but so is momentum. We value practical progress over perfection: someone who can implement a strong, effective control today, learn from it and continue improving it, rather than spend months developing a flawless policy that never makes it into practice.

What will you be doing?

This is a delivery role. Representative work already in flight or on the near-term roadmap:

  • Endpoint & identity security engineering - contributing to the CrowdStrike AU→UK CID migration (Intune-deployed, scripted), Entra ID configuration for the new EU/UK tenant, and Intune/MDM policy build-out.

  • Network security delivery - hands-on work on Netskope deployment for SaaS/web steering, Tailscale ACL and zero-trust access design, and FortiGate/UniFi security configuration for the Winnersh Triangle site.

  • Site security build - working the physical/technical security side of the Winnersh Triangle stand-up: access control (Paxton), CCTV, structured cabling security, vendor delivery oversight (we're mid-RFP with Safeguard Systems and FTL Secure Solutions) - this is real vendor and project management, not paperwork.

  • Documentation that's useful, not performative - technical runbooks, architecture diagrams, and control evidence that the team actually uses, versus policy for policy's sake.

You'll be a second pair of hands and a second brain on all of this - someone the IT Manager can hand a problem to and trust it gets solved, not just assessed.

The mindset matters more than the checklist:

  • You'd rather fix the thing than write a memo about the thing.

  • You’ll need to “muck-in” with the team if the need arises for any & all technology issues.

  • Network security fundamentals (FortiGate or similar UTM/firewall, VLAN segmentation, secure site network design)
